incomplete_fix_quote: This vulnerability [CVE-2018-17456] is very similar to CVE-2017-1000117, as both are option-injection attacks related to submodules. ... This attack works in a similar way, except that the option-injection is against the child git clone itself. Due to the similarity to CVE-2017-1000117, [GitHub] also audited all of the .gitmodules values and implemented stricter checks as appropriate.
mechanism: A .gitmodules submodule value beginning with '-' is passed verbatim as an argv element to a child process during `git clone --recurse-submodules`. CVE-2017-1000117 (fixed 2.14.1) guarded only the connect.c side (the spawned ssh: host/port/path), rejecting a leading-dash ssh host. It did NOT guard the argv of the recursively spawned child `git clone` itself; a submodule `url` value beginning with '-' (e.g. `-u/payload` == `--upload-pack=/payload`) is still parsed as an option by that child clone (CVE-2018-17456). A ':' in the submodule path routes the positional through the upload-pack transport so the override program executes. CVE-2018-17456 (fixed 2.19.1) inserts `--` before <url>/<path> in builtin/submodule--helper.c clone_submodule() and adds a warn-and-refuse for dash-leading submodule values.
